item.title: MultiChoice cuts entry-level DStv, GOtv subscriptions to ₦6,000
item.description: MultiChoice Nigeria has introduced restructured DStv and GOtv subscription packages, with entry-level options starting at ₦6,000, following customer feedback on affordability and content preferences. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho, disclosed this during an interview on the Global Business Report on ARISE News on Friday, saying the new packages were designed to simplify subscription choices and provide customers with access to entertainment, sports and other content. She said the company had listened to its subscribers and adjusted its offerings to better address their needs. “We recognised that our customers are dear to us, so we listened to our customers, we simplified our offerings,” she said. Under the new arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv offers Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. Omotosho said the Starter package, which costs ₦6,000, provides access to more than 90 channels, including Africa Magic Plus, the Premier League Match of the Week, selected UEFA Champions League matches and La Liga coverage. She also explained that the Sports package had been redesigned from the former Compact offering to provide broader access to major sporting competitions. According to her, the package includes all Premier League and Champions League matches, as well as UFC and WWE content, alongside channels available on the Starter and Select packages. Clarifying the subscription rates, Omotosho said the Sports package costs ₦21,000 for new subscribers, while the ₦19,000 rate applies only to existing Compact subscribers migrating to the new package. “When you move into the new pack, it’s ₦21,000 on the Sports pack,” she said. The CEO also highlighted the benefits of MultiChoice Nigeria’s integration into the Canal+ Group, which operates in more than 70 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe. She said the integration had strengthened the company’s capacity in content acquisition, technology and partnerships while retaining its focus on the Nigerian market. “We’re basically riding on global muscle, but we still want to be very relevant to the Nigerian consumer,” she stated. On the company’s transition towards digital entertainment, Omotosho said MultiChoice regarded satellite television and streaming services as complementary platforms rather than competing products. “For us, streaming is not an ‘either/or,’ it is ‘and’,” she said. She cited DStv Stream, which enables subscribers to access television content online without a satellite dish or decoder. According to her, the company’s technology-agnostic approach allows customers to choose satellite television for reliability in areas with limited broadband access or streaming services for greater flexibility. item.title: AI-generated fake content threatens democracy, national security – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as disruptive as a very dangerous weapon.” He said the 2023 general elections were an example of the dangers of irresponsible communication, adding that although social media facilitated political mobilisation, it also enabled the circulation of fabricated election results, unverified claims and divisive ethnic and political narratives. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. He said: “In an age of unprecedented information flow, the credibility, integrity and social value of what we communicate are as important as the freedom and the platforms through which we communicate.” The airline chairman also cited the COVID-19 pandemic, when the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic of false and misleading information that confused populations, encouraged risky behaviour and weakened confidence in public health institutions. He said misinformation surrounding Ebola outbreaks in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo similarly fuelled distrust of health workers and undermined disease-control interventions. “These examples demonstrate that irresponsible communication can threaten not only democratic stability but also human lives,” he warned. item.title: ASUU Suspends Taraba Varsity Strike After Gov Kefas’ Intervention
item.description: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University chapter, has conditionally suspended its ongoing strike. The union resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on 12 October 2026, with effect from 20 November 2026, following Governor Agbu Kefas’ approval of the full implementation of the 2025 agreement between the Federal Government and ASUU. The decision was reached at a congress held on Friday to determine the union’s position on the governor’s appeal for the suspension of the industrial action and his approval of the agreement’s implementation. This was contained in a statement issued by the ASUU chairman at Taraba State University, Garba Mbave. ASUU-TSU had embarked on the strike over the Taraba State Government’s failure to implement the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU remuneration agreement and pay outstanding salary arrears accrued from January 2026. The union had earlier engaged the state government on the demands, but commenced the indefinite industrial action on October 12 after efforts to resolve the dispute failed. A file photo of Governor of Taraba State Agbu Kefas. Photo: Facebook/Agbu Kefas The union expressed profound appreciation to Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their interventions, constructive engagement and commitment towards resolving the industrial dispute. The union also appreciated members of the public, students, parents, staff and the entire university community for their patience, understanding, solidarity and cooperation throughout the strike. “The support, restraint and confidence demonstrated during this challenging period are highly appreciated. The Union acknowledges the sacrifices and inconveniences occasioned by the strike and appeals for continued understanding and cooperation as efforts towards the restoration of normal academic activities and sustainable industrial harmony are pursued,” the statement said. ASUU Logo ASUU reaffirmed its commitment to industrial harmony, constructive dialogue and the restoration of normal academic activities, while stressing the need for the faithful implementation of the resolutions reached. It urged the Taraba State Government, the university management and all relevant parties to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the full and timely implementation of the resolutions contained in the communiqué and the Memorandum of Action (MoA). “The sustainability of industrial harmony and the uninterrupted academic calendar depend on mutual trust, accountability and strict adherence to agreed commitments. “Accordingly, all parties are urged to honour their respective obligations to prevent a recurrence of the dispute and safeguard the interests of staff, students, the University and the wider education sector,” the statement added. item.title: United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri
item.description: United Nigeria Airlines will commence scheduled flight operations from Jos to Lagos, Kano and Owerri on November 24 and 29, 2026, providing residents of Plateau State with additional air connections to other parts of the country. The airline said tickets for the new routes were already available for purchase. The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while the Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos routes will each operate twice weekly. Flights between Jos and Kano will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while those between Jos and Owerri will run on Wednesdays and Sundays. However, because the Owerri airport is currently closed, operations on the Jos–Owerri route will commence on Sunday, November 29, five days after the initial launch date. The development follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines on Monday, November 9, at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, the airline will introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, which the state government said were previously not served. Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership was part of the state government’s broader efforts to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunities. He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s vision. According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will ease movement between Plateau and the South-East and South-South regions, thereby supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchanges. He said the Jos–Kano connection would further strengthen Plateau’s relationship with the North-West, which he described as home to major commercial and industrial centres offering opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement was significant because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. He described Plateau as a strategic state and assured that the airline would maintain its service standards. Okonkwo also commended Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, while acknowledging Gyang’s efforts in facilitating the agreement. Passengers can book flights through the airline’s website, mobile application or accredited travel agents. The post United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: University of America challenges NUC over illegal operations
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The National Universities Commission (NUC) and the University of America, Curaçao, have disagreed over the legality of the institution’s academic operations in Nigeria, with the commission warning prospective students against seeking admission into its programmes. The NUC had declared the institution’s operations in Nigeria illegal, alleging that it was admitting students, running academic programmes and claiming to award degrees through unauthorised campuses and learning centres across the country. However, the university has challenged the commission’s position, insisting that its legal existence as a foreign institution is distinct from the regulatory status of its learning support centres in Nigeria. In a public notice issued on Tuesday, the NUC’s Director of Public Affairs, Rita Okonjo, said the institution, also known as the University of America, had not been authorised to operate or award degrees in Nigeria. She identified the centres allegedly linked to the institution as Cosmopolitan International Business School (CIBS), Garki, Abuja; its purported Federal Capital Territory learning centre; and the University of America College of Science and Technology, also known as UAPOLY, Ekpoma, Edo State. Okonjo said the commission’s investigations showed that the institution was not accredited by any agency recognised by the United States Department of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA). She explained that its purported listing in the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), as well as claimed registrations in California and Florida, did not constitute accreditation or authorisation to award recognised university degrees. The NUC spokesperson also dismissed claims that the institution had obtained approval from the Federal Ministry of Education, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, the National Board for Technical Education and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. According to her, even if such approvals had been obtained, they would not confer the authority to operate a university or award degrees in Nigeria. The commission expressed concern over advertisements by the institution offering programmes in law, nursing science, engineering, pharmaceutical science, aerospace and rocket engineering, as well as postgraduate qualifications, including PhD degrees. It also raised concerns about promises of National Youth Service Corps mobilisation, professional recognition and opportunities to obtain green cards to live and work in the United States or Europe. Okonjo warned that qualifications obtained from unapproved institutions would not be recognised for NYSC mobilisation, professional registration with relevant Nigerian regulatory bodies or admission into the Nigerian Law School. item.title: Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis
item.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS — The Fountain of Life Church has denied reports that its premises have been sealed, insisting that the church remains open, although access to its facilities is currently restricted amid an ongoing leadership dispute. The church, in a post on its official Instagram page, shared a graphic bearing the inscription, “DON’T BELIEVE THE NOISE! CHURCH IS NOT SEALED,” while inviting worshippers to attend its Sunday service. The clarification comes amid a leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the church’s board, which has generated public attention in recent days. However, a visit by Vanguard correspondents to the church premises revealed restricted access, with activities appearing limited. There was no visible presence of police personnel at the premises, while private security operatives were stationed at the entrance. Efforts by a Vanguard reporter to gain access to the church were unsuccessful, as a security official said only persons with official business within the premises would be allowed in. The restricted access comes despite the church’s public invitation to worshippers to attend Sunday’s service. The church had earlier announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, initially scheduled for Sunday, November 22, stating that a new date would be communicated. The developments come against the backdrop of a legal battle over the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had restrained Odukoya from holding himself out as Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the trustees. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other operations. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application. However, the court preserved his right to apply to set aside the orders or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership dispute became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid. item.title: Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels. The post Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: European leaders urge Russia to halt winter energy attacks
item.description: …Back ceasefire, security guarantees for Ukraine By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine have called on Russia to suspend attacks on energy facilities throughout the winter, describing an energy truce as a first step towards ending hostilities in Ukraine. The leaders also called for a ceasefire to facilitate food exports through the Black Sea, stressing that safe passage for ships was critical to global food security. The position was contained in a joint statement shared by the German Embassy in Nigeria on Friday, following a meeting in Berlin on Thursday involving Ukraine, the United States and members of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries supporting Ukraine. The leaders condemned what they described as an escalation in Russian missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian civilians and civilian infrastructure, while expressing condolences to the families of victims. They reaffirmed their solidarity with Ukraine and its right to defend itself against Russia’s invasion, insisting that continued attacks would not weaken their support for Kyiv. The statement said the countries would work with other partners to provide Ukraine with additional missile defence systems before winter, particularly those capable of intercepting ballistic missiles to protect civilians and critical infrastructure. The leaders also backed direct talks between Ukraine and Russia, with the participation of the United States and European countries, and welcomed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s willingness to accept an immediate ceasefire and engage in meaningful negotiations. They, however, insisted that any peace agreement must respect Ukraine’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and right to determine its security arrangements and alliances. According to the statement, proposals concerning the European Union or NATO would require the consent of their respective members. The leaders further called for legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine once a ceasefire takes effect. The proposed arrangements include a US-led mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire and a European-led multinational force supported by the United States. Other measures could include continued military, financial and technical assistance to Ukraine, as well as a legally binding commitment, subject to national procedures, to take steps to restore peace and security if Russia launches another armed attack. On military assistance, the leaders reaffirmed a pledge by NATO allies to provide €70 billion in military equipment, assistance and training in 2026, with at least the same level of support in 2027. They also said the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan would provide €90 billion in military and financial assistance by the end of 2027. The countries pledged to work with Ukraine on agreed reforms, particularly strengthening the rule of law and combating corruption. item.title: Taraba varsity ASUU suspends strike conditionally
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University (TSU) Branch, has conditionally suspended its ongoing industrial action with immediate effect, paving the way for the resumption of academic activities. The union announced the decision in a statement issued on Friday and signed by its Branch Chairman, Dr Joshua Garba Mbave. It said its Congress, at an emergency meeting held at the ASUU-TSU Secretariat in Jalingo, resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on October 12, 2026. According to the statement, academic activities will resume from November 20, 2026. However, the union warned that the restoration of industrial harmony and the sustenance of an uninterrupted academic calendar would depend on mutual trust, accountability and strict compliance with agreed commitments. ASUU-TSU urged the Taraba State Government, the university management and other relevant stakeholders to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the timely and full implementation of all resolutions contained in the joint communiqué and Memorandum of Action (MoA). It warned that failure to honour the agreements could lead to a recurrence of the dispute. The union expressed appreciation to Governor Agbu Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their engagement and intervention in resolving the impasse. It also thanked students, parents, staff and the wider university community for their patience, solidarity and understanding during the five-week industrial action. The union appealed for continued cooperation as normal academic activities resume. The post Taraba varsity ASUU suspends strike conditionally appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Obi draws massive crowd in Onitsha, visits alma mater
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, on Friday attracted a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections. Obi began his visit with a trip to his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he addressed students and expressed optimism that the institution would produce Nigeria’s president in the future. He reminded the students that the school had produced three state governors, including former Rivers State Governor, Dr Peter Odili, himself and his successor as Anambra State governor, Chief Willie Obiano. Obi urged the students to take their education seriously, promising to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in 2027. From the school, Obi and his entourage embarked on a roadshow through major parts of the commercial city. The convoy moved from Oguta Road through the popular Upper Iweka, the Head Bridge and Uga Road before proceeding to Modebe Avenue and All Saints Cathedral, where the party’s town hall meeting was scheduled to hold later in the day. Among those who accompanied Obi during the roadshow were Aisha Yusuf and Mama P, among other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign songs and cheering the NDC presidential candidate as his convoy passed. Some of the traders reportedly closed their shops to join the gathering at the venue of the town hall meeting. item.title: Nigeria targets May for local passport production
item.description: .Set to produce 6 million passports yearly By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has begun work on a centre in Abuja that will let Nigeria manufacture its own electronic passport (e-passport) booklets for the first time, with capacity to produce six million passports a year. Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this on Friday during the ground-breaking for the National Passport Booklet Manufacturing Centre, at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Abuja. “The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 to 2 million passports a year, but by May, we will have the capacity for 6 million passports a year in production, which we are going to scale to 10 million booklets a year,” he said. The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, broke the ground. Tunji-Ojo said the plant, which will sit on 1.1 hectares, would run off the grid and be driven by artificial intelligence. “By the time we deliver it in May, Nigeria will be the first country in West Africa to do it,” he said. He added that “there are only three countries in Africa that manufacture passports in-country”, naming South Africa, Ethiopia and Algeria. Of the three, he said, only Ethiopia has the capacity to make e-passports. The minister said the facility was not being built only for Nigeria’s needs. “What we and our partners, Iris Smart, are doing is to build a passport facility that will be able to service ECOWAS and even be able to export to other countries,” he said, referring to the Economic Community of West African States. On funding, Tunji-Ojo said the government was not footing the bill. “This project is about $70 million without a dime from government,” he said, describing Iris Smart, the vendor, as “a 100 per cent Nigerian company”. The minister disclosed that the company was first awarded an e-passport contract in 2003 under President Olusegun Obasanjo, but had been importing the booklets. He said he insisted that this must change when he assumed office. “We said we cannot be aiding employment in other countries and be creating unemployment in our own country,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said there was a heated exchange with the company over the issue. “I think the first day, I walked them out of the office. I told them, you cannot have a contract for years and be importing,” he said. According to him, the company then invested more than five or six million dollars in a production centre, and is now putting about $70 million into the new plant.He said the Service’s officers would run the facility. “We have invested in knowledge transfer so that at no time will any vendor be able to hold the government of Nigeria to ransom on anything,” he said. item.title: Spain face France, England take on Norway in Nations League quarters
item.description: World champions Spain will face France while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League, after the draw took place on Friday. Spain beat France 2-0 in the semi-finals of the World Cup in the United States in July, on the way to winning the trophy. They also defeated Les Bleus 5-4 in the semi-finals of the last edition of the Nations League, last year. The quarter-finals will be played over two legs in late March, with Spain at home first after coming second in Group A3, while France topped Group A1. Spain won the Nations League in 2023 while France beat them to win the 2021 final. England topped Group A3 on goal difference after beating Spain away in their last outing, and their reward is a two-legged last-eight tie with Norway with the first leg on Norwegian soil. England edged Norway in the World Cup quarter-finals this year before losing to Argentina in the semi-finals. The other quarter-final ties pitched reigning Nations League champions Portugal against the Netherlands, and Belgium against Germany. The winners of the quarter-finals will advance to the final stages, which will be held in June in a venue yet to be decided. Spain or France will play the Netherlands or Portugal in the semis, with England facing Belgium or Germany should they get past Norway. There will also be play-offs for relegation between Leagues A and B in late March, with Wales — who finished bottom of Group A4 — fighting for top-tier survival in a two-legged tie against Slovenia. Ireland, who came second in their group in League B, will play Croatia while Denmark face Bosnia and Herzegovina and Hungary play Serbia. The four nations already promoted to League A are Switzerland, Northern Ireland, Austria and Sweden. The Nations League quarter-finals and play-offs in March will all take place at the same time as qualifying begins for Euro 2028. item.title: FIFA President Infantino Visits Warri Stadium, Pledges Support For Nigerian Football
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended the Delta State Government for its investment in the remodelling of Warri City Stadium, describing the transformation as a significant boost to football development in Nigeria. Infantino made the remarks on Friday during an inspection visit to the stadium in Warri, Delta State, alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström. He praised Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for investing in modern sports infrastructure, noting that such facilities are essential for nurturing young talents, expanding participation and creating opportunities for future generations. The FIFA president also celebrated Nigeria’s rich football heritage and its contributions to the global game, noting that some of the world’s finest footballers have emerged from the country. Infantino described the remodelled stadium as impressive, expressing enthusiasm about its facilities and his desire to play football there once the remaining work had been completed. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region. “Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said. ﻿ Expressing delight at the passion for football in Nigeria, Infantino said he was impressed by the energy and investment in the sport in Delta State. “It has been, and it is, really fantastic. I’m having a great time here. I can feel the love and the energy for football. This is Nigeria. This is Delta State. This is Warri. This is what we are all about. “This is heartbeat. It’s passion. It’s love, but it’s also investment. It is believing in the youth. It is believing in the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. He further applauded the recent triumph of Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing the achievement as a source of pride for Nigeria, Africa and the global football community. Referring to the Flamingos’ triumph in Morocco, he added, “The girls, they were just crowned world champions two weeks ago in Morocco. This is what we believe in. The boys and the girls. The future. The investment.” He congratulated the state government and other stakeholders on the project, assuring Nigeria of FIFA’s continued support. “So I’m very happy to be here. Congratulations to all of you. Thank you for everything you have done. You will always count on FIFA and on the FIFA president as your not just partner, but your family member. Thank you so much,” he said. Earlier, the FIFA president inaugurated the Hussey College Sports Complex in Warri, a grassroots sports facility donated by the Brownhill Foundation with support from the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board. It was a pleasure to welcome the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, to Osubi this morning.
